newsitem.title: GERMANY: German unions say NRW retail pay talks break down.
newsitem.headline: German unions say NRW retail pay talks break down.

text.p: Pay talks for the 500,000 employees in the retail sector in the German state of North Rhine-Westphalia broke down in the eighth round, German unions DAG and HBV said on Friday.
No date for a renewed round of talks was given.
The discussions are aimed at finding a compromise regarding extra payment for longer working times when German shop opening hours are extended later in the year, ostensibly in November.
The success or failure of the new opening hours depends on the co-operation of retail unions.
There had been optimism that the talks between employers and the employees unions DAG and the trade, insurance and banking union HBV would be successful.
However, employers' associations have distanced themselves from the original offer to pay an extra 55 percent subsidy for work after 8 p.m. local time.
The German states of Rhineland-Pfalz, Bavaria and Saarland have already reached agreement on subsidy rates for late work.
In the state of Hesse, the discussions planned for Friday morning had not started by midday, as employers said they still needed to take advice.
